clue.text: They never get drunk

parts.note: the dregs left at the bottom of a glass are the part of the drink nobody actually swallows

explanation.definitionFit: Heeltaps are the small amounts of liquor left undrunk in the bottom of glasses.

clue.text: Time is everything to these beauties

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Beautiful women for whom time means everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everything to' is padding that joins the pieces to the definition; houris are the maidens of the Muslim paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Houris are the beautiful virgins promised in the Islamic paradise, so lovely women.

clue.text: Greater Manchester's cakewalk here?

parts.note: a place in north-west England famous for a currant pastry, so a 'cake walk' could be a stroll there

explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester that gives its name to the Eccles cake, a round flaky pastry filled with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: The town near Manchester is known for its currant-filled cakes.

clue.text: The last one to make a score

definitions.text: The last one to make a score

parts.words: The last one to make a score
parts.note: a score is twenty, so the item that completes a set of twenty is the final ordinal

explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty items, and the ordinal of the last of them completes it.

clue.text: Not a lay figure

parts.note: a layman is an amateur or non-expert, so someone who is not lay is a paid expert

explanation.walkthrough: A 'lay figure' is an artist's jointed mannequin, but here 'lay' means non-expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are amateurs, so the opposite is a qualified practitioner earning a living.

clue.text: Nearly all the drink can go back

annotationWithheld.why: Nearly all the drink can go back (6): 'can go' reversed gives OGNAC, only the last five letters of the answer; the grammar cannot express wordplay that builds just 'nearly all' of the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: Nearly all the drink can go back

clue.text: Colourful sort of chore

definitions.note: adjective for a noun answer: ochre is a colour, used loosely as a describing word

indicators.note: a sort of chore means some reshaping of that word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of household task that brings colour into one's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges CHORE into the pigment name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and colour.

clue.text: He's certainly not a rank outsider

definitions.text: He's certainly not a rank outsider

parts.words: He's certainly not a rank outsider
parts.note: rank here means aristocratic rank or title, so a man inside the titled class

explanation.walkthrough: A 'rank outsider' is a racing long shot; here rank means social status.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer holds hereditary rank, so he is firmly inside the titled classes.

clue.text: Such talk sounds catching

parts.note: the word splits into a smack of hands and a snare, so it sounds like a device that catches

explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, talk meant to win applause.

clue.text: Was Stowe's hero also " cribbed and confined "?

definitions.text: Was Stowe's hero also " cribbed and confined "?

parts.words: Was Stowe's hero also " cribbed and confined "?
parts.note: Macbeth's line 'cabin'd, cribb'd, confin'd' recalls the title of Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel about a slave's cabin

explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel lived in the famous Cabin.

clue.text: A dreadful thing to have

parts.note: dreadful taken literally as full of dread: an irrational fear one suffers from

explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an intense irrational fear, literally a thing full of dread.

clue.text: As the crow flies or the horse races

definitions.meaning: in a straight line directly between two places
cross-country steeplechases for amateur riders, usually on farmland

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means directly between places, and is also the name of amateur cross-country steeplechase meetings in Britain.

clue.text: It's about an old railway losing money — so sluggish !

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the rest, so it surrounds the shortened railway

parts.note: the word it, the 's being a link

indicators.note: the railway gives up a letter, so one piece comes out of its initials

parts.note: the LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway, one of Britain's pre-1948 companies
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A complaint that a loss-making old railway runs painfully slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' is the pound sign's L, which the old London and North Eastern Railway drops; 'It's' reads as the word it plus a linking 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is inactive and slow to move, like a sluggard.

clue.text: A running match

parts.note: a couple who run off together to marry in secret make a match on the run

explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running away secretly to marry, so a match made by fleeing.

clue.text: A great parson could be a popular one

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: A fine clergyman may be well liked by his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a welcome or acceptable person.

clue.text: It has, in a roundabout way, a stabilizing effect

definitions.text: It has, in a roundabout way, a stabilizing effect

parts.words: It has, in a roundabout way, a stabilizing effect
parts.note: a spinning wheel keeps steady by turning round, so stability comes via rotation

explanation.definitionFit: This spinning-wheel device resists change of orientation and is used to steady ships and aircraft.

clue.text: They're' not out to do good turns.

definitions.text: They're' not out to do good turns.

parts.words: They're' not out to do good turns.
parts.note: swindlers who twist things do turns, but not kind ones

explanation.definitionFit: Twisters are cheats or swindlers, though the word also means things that turn.

clue.text: How to make a tiny tree last for all time

indicators.note: the clue asks how to form something, meaning the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a small sapling alive for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to make' rearranges TINY TREE; 'last for' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless duration, time without end.

clue.text: Charming operators!

parts.note: charming taken literally as using charms or spells, of people who heal

explanation.definitionFit: These tribal healers work by spells and charms rather than medicine.

clue.text: Churchman going twice to the dance

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used for an encore
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A clergyman going to the dance twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior clergyman in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: Fish we associate with rollers ?

definitions.meaning: flat rays of the sea, a kind of fish
footwear with wheels, as in roller boots

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat seafish and the bladed or wheeled boots used on rinks.

clue.text: She liked the bottle left on the chimley-piece

definitions.text: She liked the bottle left on the chimley-piece

parts.words: She liked the bottle left on the chimley-piece
parts.note: Dickens's tipsy nurse in Martin Chuzzlewit asks for the bottle to be left on the chimney-piece

explanation.definitionFit: The drunken nurse in Dickens's novel Martin Chuzzlewit, with her famous bottle.

clue.text: Where to put up the drunken helot

indicators.note: a drunken word staggers about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Where to lodge an intoxicated serf.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a place offering lodging for travellers.

clue.text: By gum ! Anyone can do it !

definitions.text: By gum ! Anyone can do it !

parts.words: By gum ! Anyone can do it !
parts.note: gum is glue, so anything joined with gum is fastened, and anyone can fix things that way

explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' looks like a northern exclamation, but it means by adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to fasten with glue or paste.

clue.text: Is its sex changeable ?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase can be changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether something's gender can be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be, so the verb matches the third-person form.

clue.text: Could be a dangerous glance

parts.note: a glance taken as a glancing blow, a bullet bouncing off a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a bullet or missile rebounding off a surface, a glancing hit.

clue.text: Choice between this danger and the whirlpool

definitions.text: Choice between this danger and the whirlpool

parts.words: Choice between this danger and the whirlpool
parts.note: the Greek myth of two perils of a strait, a six-headed monster and the whirlpool Charybdis

explanation.definitionFit: The sea monster of Greek myth faced opposite the whirlpool Charybdis.

clue.text: They're always made under trying conditions

definitions.text: They're always made under trying conditions

parts.words: They're always made under trying conditions
parts.note: trying read literally as making an effort, so efforts are made whenever someone tries

explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are efforts, and are made only when one is trying.
